datasheet_id_and_revision: ADA4895-1/ADA4895-2 Data Sheet, Rev. B; document code D10186-0-4/15(B) (p24 footer, located by text search; 'Rev. B' read on rendered pages); copyright 2012-2015. Distributor-hosted copy of the manufacturer PDF. Covers the single ADA4895-1 and dual ADA4895-2.

input_type: bipolar (voltage feedback; 'XFCB3' process p16, 'SiGe bipolar process' p1); rail-to-rail output
compensation: decompensated, internally compensated; stable for G >= 10 (noise gain >= 10)

min_stable_gain.conditions: 'G >= 10 stable' (title, p1); 'minimum gain 10 stable when used in normal gain configurations' (p19)
min_stable_gain.below_minimum: p19 (Fig. 50, Table 11): an R1-C1 network from the inverting input to ground keeps the high-frequency noise gain near +9/+10 while the low-frequency gain is +5 to +9. G = +5: RT 49.9 ohm, R1 49.9 ohm, C1 60 pF, RG 49.9 ohm, RF 200 ohm, RO 49.9 ohm, CL 150 pF; resonance 1/(2 pi R1 C1) = 53 MHz; HF noise gain about +9; peaking 'a little over 2 dB' (Fig. 51); total output noise rises unless an antialiasing filter is used. Table 11 also gives G = +6 (R1 66.5 ohm, C1 45 pF, RG 40.2, RF 200, CL 150 pF), +7 (110 ohm, 27 pF, 37.4, 226, 150 pF), +8 (205 ohm, 15 pF, 32.4, 226, 120 pF), +9 (no R1/C1, RG 30.9, RF 249, CL 100 pF). For transimpedance use the capacitive noise gain (CS + CM + CF + CD)/CF must be kept greater than 10 (p21). For lower gains the ADA4897-1/-2 (unity-gain stable) is suggested (p16).

tia_content.what: Wideband photomultiplier preamplifier (I/V converter) with design equations; no numeric component example
tia_content.C_F: C_F = sqrt(C_S / (2 pi R_F GBP)) for 45 deg phase margin
tia_content.C_D_or_source_C: C_S = total summing-junction capacitance (amplifier + photomultiplier + board); C_M, C_D = amplifier common-mode and differential input capacitance
tia_content.bandwidth: f(45) = sqrt(GBP / (2 pi R_F C_S)); about 2 dB peaking and 15% overshoot; doubling C_F and halving the bandwidth gives a flat response with about 5% overshoot

tia_content.what: Noise model of the TIA: f1 = 1/(2 pi R_F (C_S + C_M + C_F + C_D)), f2 = 1/(2 pi R_F C_F), f3 = GBP/((C_S + C_M + C_F + C_D)/C_F); rms contributions: R_F sqrt(4kT R_F f2 1.57); voltage noise ven (C_S+C_M+C_F+C_D)/C_F sqrt(f3 1.57); current noise ien R_F sqrt(f2 1.57)
Stability rule for TIA use: capacitive noise gain (C_S + C_M + C_F + C_D)/C_F must be kept greater than 10; input current and its noise create offsets and output noise with large feedback resistance
Decompensated-amplifier speed argument: TIA speed scales with the square root of the GBP ratio (1 GHz GBP is 10x faster than 10 MHz)

application_guidance: Closed-loop -3 dB approx GBP x RG/(RF + RG) for gains above 10 (p16). Keep RF between 250 ohm and 1 kohm for low total noise; amplifier noise small for source resistance about 50-700 ohm (p18, Fig. 49). Gain < +10 RC network (p19). Cascaded G = +100 example with RF 226 ohm, RG 25.5 ohm, CF 2 pF (about 9 GHz total GBP, p20). Feedback capacitor reduces peaking (Fig. 54). Layout (p22): no ground plane under/around input and output pins; parallel bypass capacitors from each supply to ground, 0.1 uF 0508 ceramic close to the pins plus 10 uF electrolytic.
abs_max_and_input_protection: Supply 11 V; common-mode input -Vs - 0.7 V to +Vs + 0.7 V; differential input +/-0.7 V; storage -65 to +125 C; operating -40 to +125 C; lead 300 C; junction 150 C (Table 5, p7). Diode clamps across the inputs conduct above about 0.7 V differential: limit current below 10 mA with series resistors; ESD clamps conduct 0.7 V beyond the rails, limit fault current below 10 mA (p16). HBM 2.5 kV, CDM 1 kV.
other_notes: DISABLE: enabled above +Vs - 0.5 V (internal pull-up, may be left open), disabled below +Vs - 2 V; disabled current about 50 uA at 5 V total; enable 0.25 us, disable 6 us (Tables 2-4, p16).
inconsistencies: Junction temperature: Table 5 lists 150 C while the text (p7) mentions 'exceeding a junction temperature of 175 C for an extended period'.
Input current noise at 100 kHz: 1.6 pA/rtHz (Features, Table 2 at +/-5 V) vs 1.7 pA/rtHz (Tables 3-4, and the p18 text).
GBP 'in excess of 1.5 GHz' vs closed-loop G x BW of 2.3-2.36 GHz (with peaking) and an open-loop slope steeper than 20 dB/dec between 10 and 100 MHz.
Open-loop plot conditions are not printed; the page default (+/-2.5 V, RL = 1 kohm) is assumed.
Voltage-noise curve above a few MHz reflects the G = +25.9 measurement response (peak 1.58 nV/rtHz near 30 MHz, then falling), not intrinsic input noise.
Current noise is plotted only to 1 MHz.
